concepts.def: ∫f(x) dx = F(x) + C where F'(x) = f(x). C is the constant of integration.
∫xⁿ dx = xⁿ⁺¹/(n+1) + C for n ≠ −1. For n = −1: ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| + C.
∫sin x dx = −cos x + C; ∫cos x dx = sin x + C; ∫eˣ dx = eˣ + C; ∫(1/x) dx = ln|x| + C.
∫ₐᵇ f(x) dx = F(b) − F(a). Represents net signed area between curve and x-axis from a to b.
If f(x) ≥ 0 on [a, b], the definite integral gives the area. Negative regions subtract.
V = π ∫ₐᵇ y² dx (rotation about x-axis). V = π ∫ y² dy or π ∫ₓ² dy (about y-axis).

walkthroughs.body_html:
Integration — a core area of A-Level Maths.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Integration brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Integration.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What must you remember to include when finding an indefinite integral?
options: You always need to add 1 to the answer to account for rounding.
You don't need anything extra — the integral is just the antiderivative.
Definite integrals are negative only when the limits are reversed.
A constant of integration (+ C), because the derivative of any constant is zero.

mcqs.q: Can a definite integral give a negative value, even when integrating a function from left to right?
options: Definite integrals are negative only when the limits are reversed.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
Yes — if the function is below the x-axis over the interval, the integral is negative.
Definite integrals are always positive because area cannot be negative.

mcqs.q: What is the value of x^0 (for x not equal to zero)?
options: You always need to add 1 to the answer to account for rounding.
x^0 equals x because the zero has no effect.
x^0 equals 0 because raising something to the zero gives nothing.
1 — any non-zero number to the power of zero equals 1.
